title: Heat Pump Rebates in Burlington 2026: Up to $7,500 for Electric, Oil, Propane and Wood
desc: Burlington heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: 75% of households own, and the rate depends on whether you heat with gas.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Burlington has 73,180 households, 75% of them owners. The January low averages -7.2°C, mild for Ontario, and the rebate depends on your current fuel.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Burlington
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 19,345 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981, 73% of households in an eligible house type and 50% in detached houses. 4.1% report needing major repairs. 18% live in tall apartments, which are excluded.

A Burlington owner who wants a heat pump and insulation can combine them, but the heat pump stream and the assessment stream are separate. The heat pump stream needs no assessment, only pre-approval, while insulation and window rebates need the assessment and the dates in late 2026. Plan them separately.

The contractor submits NRCan's ASHP sizing and selection form for each outdoor unit. It records the home's loads, the planned capacity and the sizing option. The program may ask for extra justification. Ask the contractor to share the completed form so you can see the assumptions.
The January average low is -7.2°C and the 2015 to 2024 record was -26.2°C. A cold-climate model on the NRCan list will cover most conditions, and the program's performance minimums apply at -15°C.

The contractor submits the pre-installation application, waits for written approval, installs the system and files the post-installation application within 30 days. A Burlington owner should ask the contractor to confirm each step in writing and to provide copies of the approvals.

An oil-heated Burlington home must transition to an electric heat pump and arrange tank removal or emptying through a TSSA-registered contractor, and the owner signs the tank removal attestation form. Propane homes also sign it. Both then qualify for the $1,250-per-ton rate.
claim_steps: Check your fuel and whether you also plan insulation or window work.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
